overview: JPMorgan Chase earned $16.9B, or $6.14 per share, in Q2 2026 with a 23% ROTCE, as equities markets revenue rose 86% and IB fees 30%. Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised NII ex-Markets guidance to ~$96.5B from $95B and adjusted expense guidance to ~$107.5B, while Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said conditions are "getting close to as good as it gets."
keyTakeaways: Barnum said the first-half capital markets complex beat expectations by $6.5B, driving $1.5B of booked expense plus an implicit $1B for the second half.
Barnum said this quarter's equities drivers (major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean market dynamics) are statistically improbable to repeat.
Dimon elevated two co-presidents and said his succession timetable is unchanged at "several years" or "a few years," up to the board.
Barnum put excess capital at ~$40B to deploy over time, and Dimon set a 17% return goal on deployed capital, open to adjacency M&A but organic first.
financialHighlights: Net income was $16.9B and EPS $6.14 including significant items, with expenses of $27.3B (+15% YoY).
CIB revenue rose 27% to $24.9B on net income of $9.7B, with IB fees up 30%, equities up 86% and fixed income up 6%.
CCB revenue rose 8% to $20.3B with net income of $5.3B and over 500,000 net new checking accounts.
Credit costs were $2.5B, including $2.4B of NCOs and a $149M reserve build, and CET1 fell 20bp to 14.1%.
guidance: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised FY2026 NII ex-Markets to ~$96.5B from $95B, with total NII ~$105.5B and Markets NII ~$9B.
Barnum raised adjusted expense guidance by $2.5B to ~$107.5B, and Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said expense growth might slow in 2027 or 2028.
Barnum guided the card net charge-off rate to ~3.2% and kept consumer deposit growth at low single digits.
Barnum declared a $1.65 quarterly dividend effective 3Q and expects IB activity to remain healthy on a "quite robust" pipeline.

qa.question: What drove the NII ex-Markets raise, and why is Markets NII guided higher despite higher rates?
qa.answer: Barnum cited deposit balances and mix as the main driver of the $95B to $96.5B raise, implying a higher exit rate, and said lower non-interest-bearing financed assets lift Markets NII, with ~$150M shifting there from a higher CIB equity allocation.

qa.question: Isn't operating leverage positive with 15% revenue growth, and why is Troy right to run the consumer bank?
qa.answer: Barnum broke down the $2.5B expense raise into $1.5B already booked from $6.5B of capital markets outperformance and $1B added for the second half, not a revenue view; Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, agreed leverage was positive and cited Troy's analytics and operations expertise.

qa.question: Are AI efficiency gains underestimated, and what was exceptional in equities?
qa.answer: Dimon cited almost 1,000 AI use cases, about 50 important, with some areas cutting jobs 30% or 40%, but said benefits accrue to customers; Jeremy Barnum, CFO, named IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean equities and Asia activity.

qa.question: How healthy is the consumer, and why buy back stock at three times tangible book?
qa.answer: Barnum said consumer spend is solid across income segments with delinquencies a little lower than expected, and JPM buys less as price rises against ~$40B of excess capital; Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said he "made a mistake" citing $20B before.
qa.read: Answered partially; no buyback amount given.

unanswered.question: How sustainable IB and markets strength is.
unanswered.how: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, described a robust pipeline but declined to guide.

unanswered.question: Where JPM is in the investment cycle and what it means for medium-term operating leverage.
unanswered.how: Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, called it a "complete continuation" with no operating leverage outlook.

droppedTopics: Private credit exposure and systemic risk
whatChanged.toneShift: Last quarter Barnum called the $105B expense guide "not a promise"; this quarter it rose to ~$107.5B, and Dimon moved from credit-cycle caution to calling conditions "close to as good as it gets."

risksMentioned: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, said yield-seeking deposit flows remain a risk in a more hawkish rate environment, and negative convexity in consumer rate paid will kick in at some point.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, described mild underwriting deterioration in some players (more PIK, weaker covenants, expense add-backs) and expects outliers in the next credit cycle.
Barnum said the negative real wage cohort is a watch area and credit depends on the labor market.
